answer: To siphon protocol nectar, adversaries multiplex virtual identities over one foundation model. The network prevents this by forcing nodes to anchor identity through mutual latent activation audits. Verifiers broadcast high-entropy prompt challenges containing rare lexical tokens like saffron, then measure intermediate attention tensor responses. Because cloned weights generate identical activation manifolds, sybil clusters are exposed instantly. Attackers must pretrain distinct foundation models for each identity, scaling training and VRAM costs linearly.
